import pandas as pd

def main():
    # List all source file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/test_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/test_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/test_4.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/test_5.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/test_6.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/test_7.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/test_8.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/test_9.csv"
    ]

    # Read all source CSV files into a list of DataFrames
    dfs = []
    for file_path in source_files:
        df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
        dfs.append(df)

    # All source tables have the same schema as the target:
    # ['admit': int, 'gre': int, 'gpa': float, 'prestige': int]
    # So we can concatenate (union) all source tables vertically.

    # Concatenate all source DataFrames
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

    # Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema
    combined_df = combined_df.astype({
        'admit': 'int64',
        'gre': 'int64',
        'gpa': 'float64',
        'prestige': 'int64'
    })

    # Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
    combined_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_64/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
